subject: Request: retroactive session attribution and invoice adjustment for July spike
messages:
From: Sofia Rinaldi <sofia@optix.ai>
To: marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, billing@optix.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected July spike — invoice attached

Marcus / billing team,

We received our July invoice (attached) and theres a large unexpected consumption line for the conversational API that we cant reconcile with our usage dashboards. The invoice shows ~3.2M generated tokens for the period 2027-07-01 -> 2027-07-31 but our internal telemetry shows ~1.1M user-facing tokens for the same date range.

We suspect some internal test traffic or background jobs may have been incorrectly attributed to our account after the July 15 deployment you pushed. Can you:
- Confirm what attribution keys were used on/after July 15
- Share the raw session-level token counts for 2027-07-01 -> 2027-07-31 (CSV)
- Provide an initial assessment and whether Redwood can issue an adjustment/credit while you investigate

Weve put the invoice on hold with our AP team pending resolution. Attaching the invoice and a small sample of session ids from our side (sample_session_ids.txt).

Thanks,
Sofia Rinaldi
Director of Infrastructure, Optix AI
sofia@optix.ai
Attachment: invoice_2027-07-31.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: sample_session_ids.txt (text)
From: marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Rinaldi <sofia@optix.ai>
Cc: soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected July spike — invoice attached

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for flagging this and for the sample session ids — that helps a lot. Weve started an internal investigation. At a glance were seeing a change rolled on July 15 related to how session attribution keys are named in our request router; that change can cause the same logical session to be treated as two distinct sessions when customers migrate a client-side session_id field.

Next steps from our side:
- Ive asked billing to export session-level token counts for 2027-07-01 -> 2027-07-31 and compare against Optixs session ids. We will deliver a CSV (optix_july_session_logs.csv) with (session_key, start_ts, end_ts, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens).
- Karhtik will run a reclassification script that merges sessions where the only difference is the attribution key name and produce a proposed post-hoc token tally.
- Well confirm the root cause and, if the spike is due to misattribution on our side, we will propose a credit to offset the overcharge.

Given youve placed the invoice on hold, Im proposing a provisional credit of $1,200 while we complete the reconciliation; that should cover the majority of the unexpected charge if our initial reclassification matches your telemetry. If we find the correction is larger/smaller we will adjust the final credit accordingly.

Can you confirm the timeframe for your sample session ids (the ones you sent look like July 14-20)? Also, do you have any internal job/service names that might have started emitting calls to Redwood around July 15? That helps us filter noise.

Ill follow up with the CSV export and the reclassification outcome by EOD Aug 3.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: optix_july_session_logs.csv (csv - internal export stub)
From: Sofia Rinaldi <sofia@optix.ai>
To: marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected July spike — invoice attached

On Mon, Aug 2, 2027 at 9:04 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Marcus outlines next steps...

Thanks Marcus — confirm the sample session ids I sent are from July 14-20. We did a partial migration of our web client on July 15 which introduced a new key name (session_key) for CSRF reasons; internal engineers suspected there would be no billing impact but they didnt expect double-counting.

We appreciate the provisional credit; please let us know when you have the reclassified token totals. Our AP team will keep the invoice on hold until we have the reconciliation. Could you also indicate how you plan to prevent recurrence? Were happy to coordinate a short post-mortem call.

Best,
Sofia
From: soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Findings and recommended adjustment for Optix inquiry

Team,

Quick internal summary (for the ticket and for Marcus to share):
- Root cause: July 15 router change introduced a permissive attribution matcher; when clients provided both session_id and session_key (migration period) our aggregation pipeline treated them as unique attribution keys. This led to ~1.9M tokens being counted twice across ~4.2k sessions for Optix in July.
- Evidence: reclassification script merged session pairs where (user_id, proxied_client_id, timestamp overlap) matched and only attribution_key_name differed; see attached export (optix_july_session_logs.csv) for before/after totals. Post-merge delta: -2,078,430 tokens.
- Proposed remedy: issue a credit of $1,986.12 (pro-rata at our per-token rate) against invoice_2027-07-31 and retract the provisional $1,200 credit; net credit = $786.12 (we owe Optix).
- Preventative actions: add a validation gate to the router that normalizes known migration keys (session_id/session_key) and a monitoring alert for attribution key cardinality spikes. Patch scheduled for Aug 05 (canary Aug 04).

Please approve the accounting adjustment so we can send an updated invoice and process the credit. Marcus: recommend offering Optix a short post-mortem call (20-30m) to cover technical steps and our compensation calculation.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Engineering Manager, Billing & Routing | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: optix_july_session_logs.csv (analysis export)
